<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par157 />the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} (equivalent to ''the circumstance, the fact, that''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=11}}, 19, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=3}}, but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=15}} equivalent to ''the way in which''.<section end=par157 />

<section begin=par158 />{{GHGpar-heading|158|Causal Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|158|a}}
A complete clause, assigning the reason for statements, demands, threats, &c., sometimes follows with the simple {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=60|verse=13}} ''give us help against the adversary, and'' (for) ''vain is the help of man''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=17}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲנִי}}), 22:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=12}}, perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=10}}; or even without {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=14}}. As a rule, however, special conjunctions in various combinations are used to introduce causal clauses.

{{GHGmargin-letter|158|b}}
The most common causal conjunctions are {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן כִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}}, &c., and {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן אֲשֶׁר|translate=because}}, prop. ''on account of the fact that''; both, however, may also be shortened to the simple {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=12}}, &c., or to {{GHGheb|text=כִּי|translate=because}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=14}}, 17, &c., or to {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=49|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, 27, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=42|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, 23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=1|verse=15}}; also {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=9}}, 23. On the other hand, the simple {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫עַן}} is sometimes repeated for emphasis, {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫עַן וּבְיַ֫עַן}} (something like the German ''sintemal und alldieweil'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=10}} (without {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} 36:3); also {{GHGheb|text=עַל־אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=30}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עַל־כִּי}}<ref>Also {{GHGheb|text=כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּן}} prop. ''for therefore'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=43|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=20}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר עַל־כֵּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=27}}, always mean ''for as much as''.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=14}} ''on the ground that''; {{GHGheb|text=עַל־דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר|translate=because of the circumstance that}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַל־כָּל־אֹדוֹת אֲשֶׁר|translate=for this very cause that}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=8}}. But just as the simple {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן}} is used for {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן אֲשֶׁר}}, so also the simple {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} with the perfect stands for {{GHGheb|text=עַל־אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=136}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=11}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=עַל־בְּלִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=20}} and {{GHGheb|text=מִבְּלִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=55}} both with the perfect, equivalent to ''because... not''.—Cf. further {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫קֶב אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=6}}, all with the perfect, and {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫קֶב כִּי}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=10}} with the perfect; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=12}} with the imperfect) prop. ''in return'' for the fact ''that''; similarly again the simple {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫קֶב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=24}} with the perfect, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=20|hidebook=1}} with the imperfect; finally, {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=4}} ''arising from'' the fact ''that,= because''; {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫חַת אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=21}}, &c., and {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫חַת כִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=29}} ''for the reason that''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|158|c}}
Rem. 1. The preposition {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} (''because of, on account of'') with the infinitive ({{GHGpar|114|e}}) is frequently used as the equivalent of a full causal clause; cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=3}}, 6, 13, 2:1, 6. Such a construction with the infinitive may, however, according to {{GHGpar|114|r}}, be continued by means of a finite verb, in which case {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} governs the verb as a conjunction; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=עַל־הַסְגִּירָם... וְלֹא זָֽכְרוּ|translate=because they delivered up... and remembered not}}, &c.; 1:11, 2:4; without {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=14}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|158|d}}
2. The choice of tense is regulated by the general principles stated in § 106 ff., viz. the perfect (cf. especially {{GHGpar|106|f}}) refers to causes already brought fully into effect, the imperfect to those which may contingently arise; cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=33}}, where the imperfect leaves the possibility still open that the persons addressed will perhaps escape the threatened punishments by avoiding disobedience.—Cf. further, {{GHGpar|111|h}} on the imperfect consecutive, and {{GHGpar|112|nn}} on the perfect consecutive in the apodosis to causal clauses.<section end=par158 /><noinclude>
